_comment_record_hz: Section H's mandatory high-risk list: "Mandatory for the highest-risk segments: S01+S02 (opening), S04 (tournament), X02 (build), X01 (controller/menu stress), CB-06 + CB-07 + Warden (representative combat), every band handoff +/-60 s (region transitions), X05 (save/load), S10 (finale)." This segment is on that list, so its baseline is 0.5 Hz rather than the 0.1 Hz journey default. Set by the Gate F coordinator, not a transcription choice. Cost is measured, not assumed: one readback+encode at 1920x1080 is 126.5 ms mean on this container, which at 0.5 Hz amortises to 1.054 ms/frame -- over the ~1 ms/frame line section 3 asks about. Section H requires the density here anyway; the overhead note carries the number so a reader can see what the density cost rather than being told it was free.
title: Opening: wake upstairs -> starter caught & named -> first wild catch -> road gate open
_comment: Transcribed from ralph/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md section B (span and handoff), section D (RT-01), section E.2 (CT-01), section E.5 (navigation record at objectives `opening_first_catch` and `open_road_gate`), section G (GF-02, GF-03-VILLAGE-01, GF-14-01, GF-15-01/02, GF-21-WEATHER-01) and section H (mandatory 0.5 Hz segment).
_comment_answer_prompts: Every move_to in this file leaves `answer_prompts` OFF. The schema is explicit that it 'must stay off in any segment whose subject is whether something blocks travel', and this segment's subject IS the opening's conversations -- a harness quietly answering Grandpa would hide the finding. Every dialogue below is advanced by its own explicit press step.
_comment_no_teleport: Section 0.6 / section J: production paths only, teleport is DIAG-only. Every position in this file is reached by walking.
